name: QuiX Quantum
description: QuiX Quantum builds photonic quantum processors based on silicon nitride waveguide technology, requiring no cryogenic cooling. The company has deployed over 15 systems worldwide, including 8-qubit and 64-qubit photonic quantum computers to the German Aerospace Centre (DLR), and secured EUR 15M in Series A funding to deliver a universal photonic quantum computer.

products.description: Silicon nitride waveguide-based photonic quantum processors operating at room temperature without cryogenic cooling

news.title: QuiX Quantum Installs Feed-Forward Control Unit for Universal Photonic Quantum Computer
news.excerpt: QuiX Quantum announced the first installation of its Feed-Forward Control Unit (FFCU), a hardware component designed to help the system respond to quantum measurements in real time.

news.title: QuiX Quantum Details Dedalo Roadmap for Logical Qubits and Hybrid HPC Integration
news.excerpt: QuiX Quantum released its vision of universal photonic quantum computing with logical qubits through Dedalo, a new system architecture designed to achieve practical, fault-tolerant systems that work seamlessly with classical supercomputers.

news.title: Enschede-based QuiX Quantum secures €15M to launch first universal photonic quantum computer
news.excerpt: QuiX Quantum secured €15M in Series A funding co-led by Invest NL and EIC Fund to deliver its first-generation universal photonic quantum computer.

news.title: QuiX Quantum Demonstrates Below-Threshold Error Mitigation in Photonic Quantum Computing For First Time
news.excerpt: QuiX Quantum demonstrated 'below threshold' error mitigation on a photonic quantum computer, achieving a net reduction in total errors. The project was conducted on the QuiX Bia Cloud Quantum Computing Service in collaboration with NASA's Quantum AI Lab, University of Twente, and Freie Universität Berlin.

news.title: QuiX Quantum partners with Artilux to improve photonic quantum hardware efficiency
news.excerpt: MoU integrates Artilux's GeSi photonic detectors with QuiX systems to reduce cooling and infrastructure requirements for data-centre deployments.

news.title: QuiX Quantum demonstrates below-threshold error mitigation in photonic quantum computing
news.excerpt: First European company to demonstrate a production-ready photonic error-mitigation method compatible with scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing.

news.title: QuiX Quantum Introduces PACU, a Photonic Assembly Control Unit for Scalable Quantum Systems
news.excerpt: QuiX Quantum launched PACU, a rack-mountable 3U control unit supporting up to 1,000 low-speed and 32 high-speed phase shifters, designed to standardize the photonic hardware layer for scalable quantum systems and ease data-centre integration. The launch marks a strategic shift toward becoming a full-stack, fabless quantum system vendor.

news.title: QuiX Quantum installs Feed-Forward Control Unit enabling real-time adaptive measurement for universal photonic quantum computing
news.excerpt: The FFCU combines FPGA-based processing with custom electronics to convert single-photon detector signals into phase-control actions with ~150 ns latency, enabling measurement-based quantum computation where each measurement outcome immediately dictates the next operation—a critical step toward universality in photonic quantum computing.

news.title: QuiX Quantum unveils Dedalo photonic architecture for fault-tolerant quantum computing with logical qubits
news.excerpt: QuiX Quantum released Dedalo, a three-tiered photonic quantum computing architecture targeting fault-tolerant systems built on logical qubits using CMOS-compatible silicon nitride photonic integrated circuits. The system operates at room temperature and is designed for modular integration into standard 19-inch HPC server racks.

news.title: QuiX Quantum unveils Carina — first Dutch quantum computer delivered to DLR Germany
news.excerpt: QuiX Quantum announced Carina on July 14, 2026: the world's first universal photonic quantum computing architecture designed for data-centre deployment, operating at room temperature with 8 input and 4 computational photonic qubits. QuiX delivered Carina to the German Aerospace Center (DLR QCI) in Ulm, becoming the first Dutch company to deliver a complete quantum computer to a customer.

news.title: QuiX Quantum launches Alquor 2.0 rack-mountable photonic processor platform in 8-, 20-, and 32-mode configurations
news.excerpt: QuiX Quantum launched Alquor 2.0 on August 4, 2026 — a commercial, 3U rack-mountable photonic processor platform built on silicon nitride running at room temperature, with air cooling and Ethernet connectivity. Prices range from €240 (8-mode) to €790 (32-mode), with a 20% early-adopter discount for academic orders by September 30, 2026.
